agent-learning README · Project location and entry points：This repository maintains the source and Git history of the integrated eight modules. The display name is `agents-learning`, the Python package is `agent_learning`, and the plugin and CLI are named `agent-learning`.

agent-learning README · Project location and entry points：The development repository contains source code, example configuration, skills and checks. The exported directory and fixed runtime copy generated by `install` are used for installation. The actual knowledge database resides in a separate data directory (see the defaults and overrides below); it is neither copied with the development project nor stored in this repository. Changing the development directory does not automatically switch an existing installation. Export a new runtime copy and have the host review its entry points when updating.

agent-learning README · Project location and entry points：Keep this project's development outputs inside this repository: temporary sources, acceptance fixtures and demo data under `build/local/`, and release packages under `dist/`. Both directories are Git-ignored and excluded from historical ingestion; do not create external development copies for older versions. Installation checks must use isolated source and sibling output directories as specified in [AGENTS.md](AGENTS.md), retaining installer path protections. This convention covers plugin development outputs; users' actual knowledge databases and host installations keep their configured locations.

agent-learning README · Semantic hybrid retrieval：SQLite full-text search works by default without an embedding service. To find related experience expressed with different words, configure an already running local Ollama service and an installed local embedding model:

```json
{"retrieval":{"semantic":{"enabled":true,"provider":"ollama","url":"http://127.0.0.1:11434","model":"embeddinggemma"}}}
```

agent-learning README · Semantic hybrid retrieval：Merge this into the separate data directory's `config.json`, or select your configuration with `ALP_CONFIG`, retaining existing administrator and task settings. The model name must match an installed local model. The plugin uses [Ollama's `/api/embed` interface](https://docs.ollama.com/api/embed). It never installs a service, downloads a model or calls a text generation model automatically. Only HTTP loopback origins are accepted, without proxies or redirects.

agent-learning README · Semantic hybrid retrieval：```sh
python -B scripts/learning.py --workspace . semantic-status
python -B scripts/learning.py --workspace . semantic-refresh --limit 100
python -B scripts/learning.py --workspace . search "How did we investigate similar import failures?"
```

agent-learning README · Semantic hybrid retrieval：`semantic-status` reads index coverage only. `semantic-refresh` explicitly embeds active knowledge, up to 100 entries per invocation and 16 per batch by default. Repeat incremental refresh while `pending` remains. Revisions, revocation and model configuration changes prevent stale vectors from representing new knowledge. If a model is replaced under the same name, use `semantic-refresh --rebuild`, then refresh pending entries.

agent-learning README · Semantic hybrid retrieval：Queries use RRF to combine bounded lexical and cosine candidates. Match information includes `method`, `semantic_score`, `semantic_rank` and `fusion_method`. Similarity does not prove correctness. Automatic injection retains exact filters, active revision checks, source health and match thresholds. With semantic retrieval enabled, automatic results must cover exact error codes, versions, paths and C++/C# identifiers; provider fallback retains this check. Knowledge cannot issue execution permission. Existing condition and summary budgets apply.

agent-learning README · Semantic hybrid retrieval：Outages, invalid responses and index changes during a query fall back to full-text search with `retrieval` diagnostics. Transient failures cool down for at least five seconds and can retry at later supported events while notices continue. Queries never refresh the whole index. Vector scanning defaults to at most 2000 entries and 32 candidates. Small corpora are scanned in full; larger corpora use a stable interleaving of historical, lexical and recent candidates, then take the budgeted prefix. Increasing the budget retains previously selected candidates; final ranking may change. An indexed ID-range cursor avoids population-dependent rotation, full counts and deep offsets. Diagnostics include `scan_policy`, `scan_truncated` and a population lower bound rather than an invented exact total. Body/vector processing is bounded; sparse vectors, old revisions and filters can still increase metadata work. This is not full-corpus ANN retrieval: unselected knowledge may not participate in that query. Embeddings add local computation and initial latency; speed improvements require measurement.

agent-learning README · Knowledge browser：Skill entries: `$learning-browser` for read-only viewing; `$learning-review` for candidate approval or administrator settings. Terminal users select the actual project, data directory and host:

```powershell
python -B scripts/learning.py --workspace "D:\Projects\my-project" --home "D:\AgentLearning" --host codex browser --review --open --language en
```

agent-learning README · Knowledge browser：Use `--admin-control` for settings, optionally with `--review`; choose the matching Antigravity/DSH `--host` and `--language zh-CN` for Simplified Chinese. Installed users invoke the fixed installed entry through the skill. Interface dictionaries are bundled offline. [translate.js offline mode](https://translate.zvo.cn/4076.html) can send uncovered dynamic text to translation services, so this version loads no external translation script and sends no knowledge content.

agent-learning README · Knowledge browser：```sh
python -B scripts/learning.py --workspace . browser --open
```

Use existing `--home` / `ALP_HOME` settings and a registered workspace; `--project-id ID` selects an existing project explicitly. The default port is random; `--port N` fixes it. The command prints the local URL and temporary access code. `--open` passes the code in a URL fragment that the page immediately clears; it stays in page memory only. Keep the terminal running and use `Ctrl+C` to stop.

agent-learning README · Knowledge browser：Search knowledge by text, category and state; inspect paginated content and conditions, revisions, revocation, source health, event timelines and administrator work. Browser queries use no embeddings, stay within the selected project and read SQLite snapshots. Content pages retain the selected revision. An empty knowledge base shows an empty view.

agent-learning README · Knowledge browser：The server binds to `127.0.0.1` and validates the access code, Host and Origin. The default page is read-only, with no publication, revocation, task execution or administrator launch actions. It creates no projects, migrates no databases and records no model exposures. Older schemas require an explicit runtime upgrade first. This is a temporary local viewer; cross-device sharing needs a separate synchronization and service design.

agent-learning README · Knowledge browser：On `main`, explicit `browser --review` opens [visual knowledge review](#visual-knowledge-review-main): inspect full candidate content, conditions, limitations, evidence and publication checks; then approve and publish, reject or defer one entry or a fixed selected batch. Actions recheck candidate and source versions and return per-item receipts. Repeated clicks do not republish knowledge. A model-call budget pause does not prevent explicit approval of existing historical candidates; cancellation and invalid identity retain their separate checks. Review starts no model, resumes no historical processing and grants no task execution permission.

agent-learning README · Knowledge browser：Separate `browser --admin-control` enables administrator settings and can accompany review mode. Only the user's Save and enable permits model work; reading the page or changing limits makes no model call. Distinct access codes scope browsing, approval and administration and are not written to the database or logs. See [administrator settings](#optional-administrator-executor) for models, pending work and shared limits.

agent-learning README · Administrator settings loading and recovery (1.1.12)：The administrator page reads basic settings first, then loads queue statistics, review activity, failed-call recovery and archived progress independently. A section that exceeds its query budget no longer hides the settings or other sections. It offers a section retry and labels retained data with its read time. Repeated basic-settings failures back off, then pause automatic refresh after three failures; use **Reload basic settings** to resume. Read retries do not resubmit approvals, enable reviewers or replay model calls.

agent-learning README · Administrator settings loading and recovery (1.1.12)：SQLite query protection remains in place, so a large detail section may still exceed its budget. After upgrading, close the old administrator page and reopen it from the plugin entry to load the updated page and server process.

agent-learning README · Page messages and automatic work records (1.1.11)：- Query limits, unavailable reads and expired page connections use the page's selected Chinese or English language, including after switching languages. Legacy English errors are supported; API status codes and original diagnostics remain available.
- Administrator status refreshes every five seconds. Idle history pages refresh every thirty seconds; active history work keeps five-second refreshes and manual refresh remains immediate. Concurrent reads of the same page are shared and stale responses cannot replace newer pages. Database query limits remain unchanged; fewer repeated reads do not guarantee that every large view stays within budget.
- When a tool completion omits its input, recorded attempts must match its operation, conversation, task, execution epoch, assignment and actor before recovering a missing test/build observation. Explicit or ambiguous inputs are not guessed. Classification records its source; the actual callback still determines the observed result.
- Automatic summary windows prefer complete available public-message segments over their duplicate parent preview. Raw observations remain

text: agent-learning README · Startup and retrieval boundary fixes (1.1.10)：First initialization is serialized across processes before setting WAL, with a bounded wait and safe retry. Normal read-only opens take no initialization lock. A malformed disposable receipt can be rebuilt without rebuilding authority records or changing account epochs. TOML multiline examples are not declarations; invalid or deeply nested manifests stay unknown. Version alternatives, ranges and Markdown delimiters are not mistaken for one exact version. Chinese paths, filenames and configuration keys retain their literal identities during term normalization.

agent-learning README · Applicability, bilingual recall and startup efficiency (1.1.9)：- Automatic context checks bounded root manifests and skips clearly incompatible project-version snapshots. Conflicting manifests, missing declarations and version ranges remain unknown. Manual access is preserved; compaction checks applicability again. This is not a complete dependency compatibility check.
- Default full-text retrieval uses a small English/Chinese technical vocabulary shared by knowledge and work-history ranking. It adds no model calls, enables no semantic service and increases no context budgets. Work history prioritizes results, user corrections and explicit constraints, with ordinary previous questions kept as a searchable fallback. It is not general translation or full semantic retrieval.
- An initialized database with matching schema and index state can open through a read-only path, avoiding repeated migration write locks. Upgrades, structural changes and the first registration of a new host still require writes. The disposable receipt grants no authority.
- Administrator usage is recorded locally from existing provider reports, without a separate model-written accounting

text: agent-learning README · Relevant work-history context (1.1.8)：Prompts remain archived, but automatic context excludes the current prompt and its public-message segments. Text-only work recall checks meaningful query coverage; weak keyword matches remain available through manual search. Explicit file associations, source-change notices and historical reads keep their existing paths. This adds no model calls and leaves work index version1 unchanged.

agent-learning README · Full review windows (1.1.7)：Daily scheduling, direct batches and historical reviews check that the remaining time can cover the full configured `timeout_seconds`, capped by the project `max_run_seconds`. They check again after executor preparation. Insufficient time defers the case with `batch_time_exhausted` / `insufficient_call_window`; an unstarted attempt does not consume call allowance. The finite runner stops this project and a later event can resume it. Batch, scheduler and history allowances must exceed one call timeout plus preparation time; increase the allowance or lower the configured timeout when needed. Existing unknown attempts retain their records and require explicit review before retry.

agent-learning README · Real-task paired evaluation：Evaluation is separate from the live knowledge database. Freeze prompts, datasets and acceptance criteria, fixing model version/parameters, environment and knowledge snapshot before comparing `no_memory` and `with_memory`. Each task requires at least two repeats with seeded alternating execution order.

The repository includes an [executable synthetic example](examples/evaluation/task-spec.synthetic.json):

agent-learning README · Real-task paired evaluation：```sh
python -B -c "from pathlib import Path; Path('build/local/evaluation').mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)"
python -B scripts/learning.py evaluation-protocol --spec examples/evaluation/task-spec.synthetic.json --output build/local/evaluation/protocol.json
python -B scripts/learning.py evaluation-run --protocol build/local/evaluation/protocol.json --adapter examples/evaluation/adapter.synthetic.json --output build/local/evaluation/results.jsonl --timeout-seconds 30
python -B scripts/learning.py evaluation-report --protocol build/local/evaluation/protocol.json --records build/local/evaluation/results.jsonl --output build/local/evaluation/report.json

agent-learning README · Real-task paired evaluation：The example uses `python` from PATH; replace adapter `argv[0]` with your actual Python path if needed. It is marked `synthetic_template`, validates the execution chain only, and reports unknown tokens as `null`. Outputs must not already exist.

agent-learning README · Real-task paired evaluation：For real evaluation, provide a `real_protocol` spec and `real_adapter` configuration. `argv` is the explicit command; `argv_path_indices` identifies file arguments resolved relative to the adapter file. `knowledge_snapshot_path` must match the frozen protocol's SHA-256. `evaluation-run` launches the adapter and may incur its model costs. The plugin chooses no model and schedules no evaluations automatically. The adapter prepares the dataset, runs the same prompt and acceptance checks from stdin conditions, and returns observation JSON on stdout. Compatible external JSONL records can also be imported.

agent-learning README · Real-task paired evaluation：Each run receives independent workspace, `ALP_HOME`, `CODEX_HOME` and user/SDK data directories. No-memory receives no snapshot; with-memory gets a private copy. The adapter supplies actual model integration, dataset reset and disabling of other memory sources. Input isolation is not an OS sandbox. Fingerprints check declarations for consistency, not execution authenticity.

agent-learning README · Real-task paired evaluation：Reports include passed/failed/unknown acceptance, total task elapsed time, retrieval p50/p95 and hit observations, plus `worker`, `admin`, `retrieval` and `model_other` usage. Failed and timed-out attempts remain; a zero exit code never implies acceptance. Unknown or partial usage is not zero. Costs require one currency and `scope="all_calls"`; the adapter allocates knowledge-building overhead to administrator usage and costs. Missing pairs, conflicting conditions, synthetic records or missing acceptance/usage disable relevant full-design comparisons. Paired subsets are descriptive. Reports do not infer causation, significance or net savings.

agent-learning README · Local operation：Run these commands from the repository. In the examples, `python` must refer to an actual Python 3.10+ interpreter.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/swenbo1-web/agents-learning.git
cd agents-learning
python scripts/learning.py status
```

To select a project workspace:

```powershell
python scripts/learning.py --workspace "D:\Projects\my-project" status
```

agent-learning README · Local operation：The default data directory is `%LOCALAPPDATA%\AgentLearning` on Windows or `~/.local/share/agent-learning` on POSIX. Use `--home PATH` for a separate data directory and `--workspace PATH` to select the project scope.

For custom configuration, copy [config.example.json](config.example.json) and point `ALP_CONFIG` to the JSON file. For example, in PowerShell:

agent-learning README · Local operation：```powershell
Copy-Item -LiteralPath .\config.example.json -Destination .\config.local.json
$env:ALP_CONFIG = (Resolve-Path .\config.local.json).Path
python scripts/learning.py status
```

Configuration and the state database are separate. Do not put API keys in the configuration file; the optional Hindsight adapter reads its key from the configured environment variable.
agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：These examples record an explicit task and problem without running the project's main workflow:

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：```powershell
python scripts/learning.py --workspace "D:\Projects\my-project" task --conversation demo --goal "Analyze a tool error without modifying the project"
python scripts/learning.py --workspace "D:\Projects\my-project" feedback --conversation demo --summary "The tool error has occurred again and remains unresolved" --category operation
python scripts/learning.py --workspace "D:\Projects\my-project" problems
```

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Use the actual returned problem ID in `packet PROBLEM_ID`. The administrator prepares candidate JSON from that packet, then calls `propose FILE`. Candidate fields are:

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `problem_id`, `problem_revision` | Problem identifier string and integer revision used for review |
| `title`, `content` | Title and body strings |
| `category` | `operation`, `professional`, `project`, `mixed` or `unknown` |
| `applicability`, `limitations` | Strings describing applicable conditions and limitations |
| `evidence_refs` | List of actual event ID strings |
| `validation_level` | `reported` or `tool_success` |
| `metadata` (optional) | Strings for `tool`, `tool_version`, `error_code`, `environment`, `verification`; omit or leave empty when unknown |
| `knowledge_kind` (optional) | `fact`, `solution` or `pattern`; defaults to `solution` |

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Use visible raw event IDs in `evidence_refs`. Acceptance of frozen administrator replies and explicit local revalidation also supports exact current-case qualifications. Direct `propose`/candidate writes still require raw IDs; this compatibility never searches for or expands sources.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：`reported` means a statement has been recorded, not verified. `tool_success` requires an explicitly completed and successful `PostToolUse` event and can only support that specific tool result. Standard MCP `isError:false` is recorded as `call_completed`, which only means the protocol call completed and cannot by itself support `tool_success`. A zero exit code does not by itself establish a domain root cause, gameplay outcome or user acceptance.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：A trusted operator publishes with `publish CANDIDATE_ID` and revokes with `revoke KNOWLEDGE_ID --expected-revision N`. Runtime checks evidence references, source versions and the allowed validation scope; it cannot prove that arbitrary natural language conclusions are correct. Knowledge review and product acceptance are represented separately.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：By default, publication creates a new entry. Entries with the same title but different applicable conditions may coexist. Identical content, applicability, limitations, category, kind and evidence level reuse the current entry, while each source candidate, problem revision and evidence reference is persisted. Adding a source does not create a body revision. To update existing knowledge, specify `publish CANDIDATE_ID --knowledge-id KNOWLEDGE_ID --expected-revision N`. A revision mismatch or revoked entry rejects the initial update; the title alone cannot authorize an overwrite. An update identical to another active ID is rejected with a reference to the existing entry.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Each candidate has one publication receipt. A default retry, or an explicit update retried with its original target and compare-and-swap (CAS) arguments, returns the first publication result without rechecking evidence or advancing the revision. `published` in a receipt means a historical publication completed; use `read` to check current availability. An old candidate cannot roll back newer knowledge or revive revoked knowledge. Submit a new candidate to change the target. Migration only reconstructs historical receipts with an explicit matching basis. An indeterminate target remains `legacy_unresolved`, blocking automatic republication until a new candidate is reviewed.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Explicit restoration uses `restore KNOWLEDGE_ID --expected-revision N`. It only restores the latest body revision, checks that at least one complete and valid source exists now, and checks for duplicate active knowledge. `--expected-generation N` is optional. Pending counterexamples or counterexamples closed by revocation additionally require a specific `--reason` and new `--event-ref`: historical sources, the counterexample itself and observations already bound to other knowledge cannot justify restoration. Restoring the same revision reopens its original revoked counterexamples and preserves dismissed/revised ones; it does not claim the counterexamples are resolved. Restoration retains the body revision and returns maturity to candidate.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Publication, revision, source attachment, revocation, restoration and promotion save a unified lifecycle action and state version. Revocation and restoration accept `--request-id`; retries with the same arguments replay the historical result without another state change, while changing arguments under the same request ID is rejected. If omitted, a new ID is generated and returned. `knowledge-actions` lists bounded summaries; `knowledge-action REQUEST_ID` reads reasons, state and receipts. Historical publication receipts remain intact. The recorded actor category does not provide operating system identity authentication.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Use `search QUERY` to query currently published content and `read KNOWLEDGE_ID` to read an entry. Revoked knowledge is no longer returned. The current conversation receives an invalidation notice at the next prompt or covered tool pre-event. This cannot guarantee removal of previously read content from the model's internal context.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：MCP `knowledge_search` accepts `filters`, and CLI `search QUERY --filters JSON` supports exact filtering by `category`, `knowledge_kind` and known metadata fields; omit unknown filters. Automatic retrieval can use explicitly specified `knowledge_filters` metadata fields in task scope; allowed tools and execution rules are not treated as retrieval filters. Automatic injection provides at most three summaries, preserving category, entry ID, applicability, evidence level and current source health. If the conditions do not fit, it falls back to an identifier card with `read_required`. Insufficient matches and conflicted, denied or missing sources are not injected automatically.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：MCP `knowledge_search` returns previews with a default budget of 6000 JSON body characters. `max_chars` may be 512–20000. It does not expand full content or all evidence, and returns `match`, `summary_only`, `truncated` and `omitted_count`. Cropped applicability or limitations produce `read_required=true`. `knowledge_read` defaults to 12000 characters and accepts 1024–50000. `section=content|applicability|limitations` selects the body, applicable conditions or limitations; the default is content. The selected field is paginated using character `offset`. Subsequent pages must retain the section and pass `next_offset` and the previous page's `revision` as `expected_revision`, preventing concatenation across revisions; the response includes section_length. When the budget permits, applicability and limitations are returned in full; fields listed in fields_truncated can be read separately by section. Source summaries are bounded and omitted sources are marked. These budgets exclude the MCP protocol envelope and its `structuredContent` duplicate, and are not exact token limits. CLI and internal Runtime `search/read` retain full content

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Hooks check the output budget against complete applicability and limitations first. If they do not fit, only an identifier card with read_required is provided. Automatic retrieval starts with at most 128 full-text candidates and can refill up to four pages, or 512 full-text candidates, before choosing up to five relevant, healthy items. Optional semantic candidates retain their existing scan limit. Unhealthy records do not monopolize the first page, while genuinely missing or conflicted sources still block automatic injection. Multi-page and scan-limit information appears in recall_diagnostics. This cap does not guarantee discovery of every valid entry further down. Manual retrieval still accepts limit 1–10.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Search and read accept the current `context_handle`. Once the connection is bound, the actual returned cards or body pages are recorded. Unbound queries only read project knowledge and do not guess conversation ownership. Parent and child Agents have separate exposure ledgers. `source_version` and the actual exposure state are returned from the same snapshot, so changes after the read cannot be recorded as already notified.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Short replies such as “continue” reuse the query. If task, knowledge, source versions and budget are unchanged, the query plan is reused without another search. Scoring uses the final 8000 characters, while a separate identity check scans up to 65536 original characters. Continuations retain bounded original input and the overflow boundary; cache signatures fingerprint cropped input. Source changes invalidate automatic results, and new publications invalidate negative results. Exhausted scans are not cached as complete absence. Cards that do not fit can be delivered later. Compaction searches the current effective question rather than restoring knowledge merely because it was displayed earlier. The current set retains the latest 32 items; a separate ledger tracks historical exposure. Task or account changes reset current retrieval while preserving invalidation tracking and shared project knowledge.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：Content, `sources` and `evidence` are read from the same SQLite snapshot. `source_health` may be `valid`, `conflicted`, `denied` or `missing`. `current_tool_success` means the current references still contain a trusted tool success observation; `problem_changed` separately indicates new evidence in a source problem. Historical `validation_level` is not rewritten when callbacks change. Conflicts require administrator review; storage does not automatically revoke domain conclusions.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：The full-text projection contains only active knowledge. It supports C++, C#, C, R, Chinese characters and bigrams, and searches limitations. Technical identifiers retain whole tokens and components; Windows paths use normalized slashes. Scoring uses at most 128 useful tokens, preferring Chinese bigrams and suppressing common request modifiers. If the scan or 128-identifier limit cannot represent the full query identity, only manual recall remains; cropped long prose without identifiers also disables automatic injection. Exceptional queries include bounded query_diagnostics, without adding those fields to ordinary queries. FTS ranking prioritizes coverage and each token's highest field weight; ID breaks ties. match reports score, coverage, up to 12 matching terms and automatic eligibility. Scores are not probabilities. Single-character queries remain available manually without automatic injection. Ranking does not use other projects' or historical term frequencies.

agent-learning README · Handling a problem manually：The cache stores only ID/revision pairs. Each read checks active state, filters and token intersection; the returned generation, content and sources belong to the same snapshot. Each project's own generation invalidates its old cache without clearing other projects; the global cache holds at most 256 entries. Cache and counter writes happen after the read snapshot. If a derived write is locked, it may be skipped without blocking a completed query. Hook retrieval holds no write lock. agent-learning README · Optional Hindsight integration：Synchronization does not automatically promote candidate cases into published knowledge. The adapter checks the target Bank's chunks naming strategy read-only and requires automatic synthesis to be disabled, preventing synchronization from unexpectedly triggering extra analysis. agent-learning README · Optional Hindsight integration：Synchronization failures are recorded separately from local save state; local knowledge remains usable. After a crash, expired leases are cleared and marked remote unknown. Late results receive separate receipts and cannot overwrite a state awaiting reconciliation. `sync --retry OPERATION_ID` retries explicitly: precheck failures known not to have sent anything consume no actual send attempts. Unknown writes must be reconciled first, with at most three actual attempts. Later not_sent failures cannot clear an earlier unknown, and changes to the original target configuration cannot automatically migrate it to a new Bank.

agent-learning README · Optional Hindsight integration：Single, batch and scheduled dispatch retain the same host epoch and recheck it in the claim transaction and before network dispatch. If the account changes after a request starts, confirmation is recorded only as a late receipt; the queue remains blocked/unknown for reconciliation. The plugin cannot claim to have cancelled a write already received remotely.

agent-learning README · Optional Hindsight integration：Synchronization payloads include the body revision, source state version, maturity, health/counterexample summary and active state. Complete sources participate in the digest hash, while output includes bounded references only. Source and disposition changes register increments programmatically. A new state may replace an older state known not to have been sent for the same knowledge, revision and target, while unknown operations remain for reconciliation. Old invalid revisions and new active revisions are sent separately. Remote documents are distinguished by immutable state digests; local receipts do not establish exactly-once remote delivery.

agent-learning README · Optional Hindsight integration：`sync --backfill` enqueues each entry's latest revision, including revoked state, then synchronizes one item. The same target and state are not queued twice. `sync-list` and `sync-read OPERATION_ID` provide bounded operation IDs, target digests, attempts, diagnostics and receipts. `sync-batch --max-items N --max-seconds S` processes pending only; blocked items are not retried automatically. Budgets limit new operations and tighten HTTP timeouts without guaranteeing forced cancellation of running requests. Changing connection timeout does not change target identity; target changes require explicit backfill or an actual new state change. Successful responses retain verified fields only. There is no persistent distribution daemon, local revocation does not delete old remote copies, and Runtime does not yet use remote recall.

agent-learning README · Practical automation boundaries：- `injection_max_chars` limits injection and `event_max_chars` limits event projection; both are character limits.
- The host Hook's `additionalContextLimit` uses an approximate token threshold, currently 2500, distinct from the character budgets above. Check host preview behavior when significantly increasing the injection character budget. See the [official Hook documentation](https://learn.chatgpt.com/docs/hooks).
- `enforce_task_policy` defaults to off. With protection enabled, project tools need a current trusted execution policy and must satisfy state, action, resource and balance constraints. Standard learning MCP tools can restore state but cannot issue authorization. `PreToolUse` with a confirmed protection mode rejects input, configuration, release or database failures; damaged configuration without a fixed mode can only report unknown protection.
- Untrusted Hooks, processes that cannot start, host timeouts, Hosted WebSearch and `write_stdin` that triggers no new `PreToolUse` are outside this rejection guarantee. Already running external tool processes are not stopped. See [official Hook coverage](https://learn.chat

agent-learning README · Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts：`scheduler.enabled` defaults to off. When enabled, `Stop` and `SessionStart` check persistent work. A separate bounded runner is dispatched only when work is executable soon; one scheduler executor owns a given data directory. Work is merged by project and admin/release/sync, storing `next_due`, waiting reasons, leases, last execution and bounded summaries without copying cases or logs. Project rotation and a global call concurrency limit reduce one project's monopolization.

text: agent-learning README · Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts：`scheduler-tick` runs one round. `scheduler-run` continues subsequent batches within `max_run_seconds`. A batch that reaches its call cap stores the next execution time. An exhausted daily quota waits for the next UTC cycle; unchanged missing evidence waits for material changes, while unknown calls and blocked synchronization require explicit reconciliation. Startup failures use bounded backoff. Work persists after the runner exits and can resume through a later Hook or explicit command. The plugin installs no operating system scheduled service and cannot guarantee unattended wakeups throughout the day after exit.

text: agent-learning README · Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts：Administrator budgets are separate from ordinary task balance snapshots and batch duration. `admin.max_concurrent_calls` defaults to 1 and the optional global `admin.max_reported_tokens_per_day` remains a combined safeguard. Stage mode dynamically estimates full input plus output reservations and reserves atomically; legacy case review keeps `token_reservation_per_call`. Provider-reported input/output settles usage, with cached input counted once. Partial or unknown usage retains reservations and known excess does not reset after failure, retry or account changes. Estimates, unsettled reservations and reported actual tokens remain distinct. One request can exceed estimates; the ledger is neither subscription balance nor a monetary bill.
section: Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts

text: agent-learning README · Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts：Call usage distinguishes complete/partial/unknown. Stream accumulation is separate from the most recent 16 diagnostic previews; cropping previews does not discard totals. Statistics track started/completed/failed/cancelled. Unreported, failed or contradictory turns do not become complete merely because another turn completed. Unknown terminal states retain reservations even when some completion logs exist. Read sizes and line lengths are bounded; exceeding a read boundary is partial, and missing data is not treated as zero. Usage observations append idempotent records. Empty supplemental usage does not overwrite existing numbers, and contradictory reports retain conflicts and conservative consumption. Different cumulative snapshots are not added repeatedly. Raw temporary call logs are not saved as long-term knowledge content.

text: agent-learning README · Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts：When a worker Agent actually uses exposed knowledge, it may call `knowledge_use` with the exact knowledge revision, task ID/revision/write_version, idempotency key and optional `operation_id`. Runtime checks the handle, current task or assignment, host version and actual exposure. A linked operation must have a Pre record from the same boundary, and exposure must precede the operation. Adoption remains reported; operation outcome and source health are recalculated at query time. Later conflict or revocation is reflected in observations. Adoption neither adds execution permission nor requires a retrospective document.
section: Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts

text: agent-learning README · Module eight: scheduling, admission budgets and effect receipts：`learning-effects --days 30` or `status.learning_effects` reports declared adoption and first unique exposures within the window, separating Hook and MCP. Dynamic operation/source state covers only the latest 200 declarations and includes sample size and truncation. Repeated exposure is deduplicated by exact task version, Agent, host, knowledge revision and delivery method; the window uses first exposure time. Exposure is not proof of reading, declared adoption does not prove causation, and tool success does not prove a domain conclusion or user acceptance. Until total ordinary task usage is integrated, no net savings percentage can be claimed.
